take_homes: Ask what job the teammate is trying to get done and what they use now before I decide what to share. I'd normally start from what I built.
Giving access is easy. Whether they take it up depends on trust and on someone they trust having used it, and when I hand it over the accountability stays with me.
Write the people plan next to the technical plan. If the people file is full of blanks, that is the finding.

monday.move: Ask one sales lead how they prep for customer calls today, and don't show them anything.
monday.who: head of sales, or whoever actually does the prep
monday.stop_condition: If they say they have no pain here or can't name who would maintain it, I don't build the org-wide setup.
monday.blocker: Nobody outside engineering asked for it, and I still haven't picked who would maintain it. I may skip the question and build it anyway.

misconception.why: The module is about sharing, not verifying. 'It has to be right the first time they try it' made me see that non-engineers can't be handed unchecked output, but I would still skip the review step on my own work. The unrequested-weekend-build habit did get a dent from the story.

one_line: decent for the 'who asked for this' blind spot and the pre-mortem, but half of it is paste a prompt and read a file, and i skimmed those parts.
